title: A shape that was turned into a picture and undone answers Backspace again
goal: Turn a rectangle into a picture, take a piece out of it with a marquee, then undo twice. The rectangle is a shape again on screen, but drawing a marquee over it and pressing Backspace now does nothing at all and says nothing: no piece comes out, and no line appears at the bottom of the canvas explaining why. A person is left pressing a key that has silently stopped answering. It should refuse out loud the way it does for any other shape.
notes:
Reproduced on the probe built from 59289581, three times, each on a locked Mac with PHOTONZ_ALLOW_LOCKED_WALK=1 (no step in the reproduction asks accessibility for a name, so the lock is not in it).

The smallest reproduction, /tmp/undo-turn-probe2.json: blank 1200x800; rectangle tool; drag (600,160) to (900,380); select tool; escape; selectRow Rectangle; rightClick Rectangle choose "Turn Into Picture…"; press "Turn Into Picture" in the sheet; rectSelect; drag (600,160) to (700,380); delete (a piece comes out, expectNotice absent passes); escape; undo; selectRow Rectangle; rectSelect; drag (600,160) to (750,380); delete; expectNotice says "Only a picture can have a piece taken out".
  -> step 34 (expectNotice): no pill is up under the canvas, so it cannot be saying "Only a picture can have a piece taken out"

It is not the undo alone and not the refusal in general:
- ONE undo (turn into a picture, undo, marquee, Backspace) raises the refusal correctly: same walk without the piece removal, status ok.
- A plain rectangle that was never turned raises it correctly: /tmp/refusal-probe-walk.json, status ok.
So the state is only reached by undoing the piece removal AND the turn.

The key really does nothing: rendering the document before and after that Backspace gives a pixel-identical picture (PIL ImageChops.difference bbox None), so the layer is not quietly being sliced either. RegionSliceRefusal.refusal(for:action:) is driven by RegionTarget.canSlice and layer.imageRef, so the layer is probably coming back from undo with an imageRef that still reads as a picture while nothing can be cut out of it.

turn-two-shapes-into-pictures-walk is the walk that catches it, at its last expectNotice. That walk was also corrected on 2026-09-20 (it drew its second marquee with nothing picked, because the escape before it drops the selection; it now picks Rectangle 2 first). It still fails, on this.
acceptance: After turning a shape into a picture, taking a piece out with a marquee, and undoing twice, a marquee plus Backspace on that layer raises the refusal line that names the layer and says what to do instead
turn-two-shapes-into-pictures-walk passes twice on its own
A walk covers the same sequence on a single layer, since that is the smallest case that shows it
